conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through a short screening tool called the EPDS, which helps us understand how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. It’s simply a way to check in on your emotional well-being, not a test of your parenting or a judgment of you in any way. Everything we discuss stays confidential, and my goal is to create a safe, comfortable space where you can be honest about the past week.

We’ll go through ten questions together. I’ll ask each one conversationally, and you can answer however feels most natural—there are no right or wrong responses. When you’re ready, we can begin with the first one:

Over the past seven days, have you still been able to look forward with enjoyment to things, or has that pleasure been hard to find?

Honestly? Most things feel kind of… flat. I used to get excited about little stuff—coffee with a friend, a new episode of my show—but now it feels like I’m just going through the motions. Every so often I’ll have a small moment where I think “oh, this could be nice,” but the spark fizzles fast. It’s like the color’s been drained out of everything I used to enjoy.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I can still laugh sometimes—like when my husband makes that silly face with the burp cloth on his head—but it doesn’t come as easily or feel as good as it used to. Mostly I’m just tired, and even the funny moments feel kind of muted.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I’ll catch myself thinking, “Maybe tomorrow I’ll feel excited about that walk or that show,” but when the time comes, it just feels… meh. It’s like I remember I used to enjoy stuff, but the actual feeling doesn’t show up anymore.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah, I do that a lot. If the baby’s fussy, I immediately think it must be something I ate or that I’m not soothing him right. When I can’t get him to nap, I keep replaying what I did wrong. Even little stuff—like spilling a little pumped milk—makes me feel like I’m failing him. The guilt just piles on even when people tell me it’s not my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much all day, every day. I’ll be feeding her and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure she’s not breathing—so I’m poking her foot every two minutes to check. Or I’ll lie awake running through horror stories about SIDS or choking or the house catching fire, even though nothing’s happened. I know the worries aren’t logical, but I can’t turn them off.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes it hits me out of nowhere—like this sudden wave of dread. My chest feels tight and I can’t catch my breath, even if the baby’s fine and the house is quiet. It’s like my body’s sounding an alarm when nothing’s actually wrong. It usually passes after a few minutes, but it’s scary while it lasts.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah. Between feedings, the piles of laundry, the texts I haven’t answered—sometimes it feels like I’m drowning in little tasks I can’t keep up with. I’ll stand in the middle of the living room just staring, not sure what to tackle first. I still manage the basics—baby’s fed, diapers changed—but everything feels heavier, like I’m wading through thick water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

That’s been happening a lot. I’ll finally get the baby down, crawl into bed myself, and then my brain just starts spinning— replaying the day, worrying about tomorrow, feeling guilty that I didn’t do enough. Even when I do drift off, I jerk awake at every tiny sound, sure he’s crying. Some nights I lie there for hours watching the clock change, feeling this heavy sadness settle on my chest.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… most of the time, really. It’s like a gray cloud that just follows me around. I’ll be holding the baby and tears start welling up for no clear reason. People keep saying “you must be so happy,” but inside I just feel empty and weepy, like I’m mourning something I can’t name.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve cried three times this week—once when the bottle of pumped milk tipped over, once when my mom said I looked tired, and once in the shower where no one could hear me. It’s like the tears are right under the surface and any tiny thing can push them over the edge.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, nothing like that. I feel low and overwhelmed, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel like me again—like I can handle being a mom without this heavy sadness.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 23: Screening Note – Postpartum Period

Symptoms endorsed
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness (“gray cloud,” crying ≥3×/week)
- Marked anhedonia (muted pleasure, anticipatory enjoyment absent)
- Excessive guilt/self-blame re infant care
- Generalized anxiety, catastrophic worries (SIDS, choking, fire)
- Panic-like episodes (sudden dread, chest tightness, breathlessness)
- Overwhelm, “drowning” in daily tasks
- Sleep disturbance driven by ruminations, hypervigilance to infant sounds

Pattern
Symptoms present most days, interfere with functioning; no self-harm ideation reported.

Screening significance
High endorsement of items consistent with postpartum depression and comorbid anxiety; no current safety concerns.
